feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Judge orders Tennessee to preserve evidence in failed execution
entry.summary: Lawyers for Christa Pike, the woman who survived an execution in Tennessee, were in court Wednesday as she regained consciousness.

entry.title: Judge orders that Christa Pike execution evidence be preserved
entry.summary: A week after the failed execution, Pike is awake but is said to be angry and confused. Her lawyers said Wednesday's hearing was about "transparency."

entry.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
entry.summary: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

entry.title: How Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has brought the culture wars to the military
entry.summary: The New York Times reporter Greg Jaffe says Hegseth has disproportionately blocked promotions of Black and women senior officers, and he's also been purging the military of transgender people.

entry.title: Over 1,000 children are buried at juvenile detention centers nationwide
entry.summary: Researchers uncovered the graves of more than 1,000 children next to juvenile detention facilities in 29 states. At one Maryland gravesite, 230 Black boys are buried.

entry.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
entry.summary: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.

entry.title: 5 things civil rights data says about public schools
entry.summary: The federal Civil Rights Data Collection, for the first time in decades, tells us about the teacher workforce and reminds us racial disparities are still stark in American public schools.

entry.title: Deep in Appalachia, a rail-to-trail project builds bipartisan support for a bridge
entry.summary: The Trump administration has been hostile to federal spending on bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure. But there's bipartisan support for a multiuse trail that would connect Ohio and West Virginia.

entry.title: Cornell students plan sit-in to protest handling of former student's rape allegations
entry.summary: Former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will lead an independent inquiry into Cornell's handling of a former student's rape allegations. Students are preparing for a sit-in Wednesday.

entry.title: Former Tennessee prisons chief also oversaw botched executions in Arizona
entry.summary: Before Tennessee's prisons chief stepped down in the aftermath of a horrific failed execution, he oversaw botched executions in Arizona. A review of protocols there spelled out serious issues.
